summaryBox.title: Exam Trap Highlights
summaryBox.takeaway: Molarity changes with T; IUPAC STP V_m is 22.71 L; LR is based on n/coeff; 1 amu = 1/12th ¹²C; H2SO4 has n-factor = 2.

conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Trap 1**: *Molarity is constant with temperature.* → Reality: Molarity decreases as T increases due to volume expansion.
• **Trap 2**: *At STP, 1 mole is 22.4 L.* → Reality: Current IUPAC STP (1 bar, 0°C) is 22.71 L/mol.
• **Trap 3**: *LR is smallest initial mass.* → Reality: LR is minimum of initial moles divided by coefficient ($n_i / \text{coeff}$).
• **Trap 4**: *Vapor density equals molar mass.* → Reality: $\text{Molar Mass} = 2 \times \text{Vapor Density}$.
• **Trap 5**: *1 amu is mass of 1 hydrogen atom.* → Reality: 1 u is 1/12th mass of neutral ¹²C atom (1.66054 × 10⁻²⁴ g).
• **Trap 6**: *Definite proportions holds for Berthollides.* → Reality: Non-stoichiometric compounds violate Proust's Law.
• **Trap 7**: *Mixing equal volumes of 1 M HCl and 1 M H₂SO₄ gives 1 M H⁺.* → Reality: $[\text{H}^+] = \frac{1(1) + 2(1)}{1+1} = 1.5\text{ M}$.
• **Trap 8**: *Equal masses of O₂ and N₂ contain equal molecules.* → Reality: $M_{\text{O}_2} = 32, M_{\text{N}_2} = 28 \implies n_{\text{N}_2} > n_{\text{O}_2}$.

quickRevision: Always check 1 bar vs 1 atm for gas molar volume.
Account for acid basicity/n-factor in mixtures.
Molality is per kg of solvent, not solution.
